style="text;html=1;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=top;whiteSpace=wrap;fontColor=#8c8f98;fontSize=11;fontFamily=IBM Plex Sans;spacing=0;" value="Submit inserts the accepted-jobs row first, then publishes the pointer message (a CloudEvent), and the reconciler republishes rows that have no publish receipt. One unique constraint on tenant and submission key dedups at submit. Temporal owns job lifecycle, Postgres holds the row of record and the event history is append only. The envelope carries identity and refs, never accumulated state. Object storage keeps one bucket per data class: sources, components, results and checkpoints. A worker uploads bytes and returns references, and the workflow commits the accepted attempt, so a late attempt never changes what a consumer reads. The reaper is a Temporal Schedule and the only role that deletes. The app database, the object store, Temporal and its database share the infra node, which is 6,144 MiB on ci with a 5,780 MiB namespace quota." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="100" width="920" x="20" y="724" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div: Submit inserts the accepted-jobs row first, then publishes the pointer message (a CloudEvent), and the reconciler republishes rows that have no publish receipt. One unique constraint on tenant and submission key dedups at submit. Temporal owns job lifecycle, Postgres holds the row of record and the event history is append only. The envelope carries identity and refs, never accumulated state. Object storage keeps one bucket per data class: sources, components, results and checkpoints. A worker uploads bytes and returns references, and the workflow commits the accepted attempt, so a late attempt never changes what a consumer reads. The reaper is a Temporal Schedule and the only role that deletes. The app database, the object store, Temporal and its database share the infra node, which is 6,144 MiB on ci with a 5,780 MiB namespace quota.
